abstract:
<jats:p>Due to non-availability of proper diet (nourishment) to the fetus after conception the fetus suffers from demise and expulsion of ama garbha are due to disorders of fetus in opinion of Bhela. Folic acid plays a vital role in embryogenesis, DNA synthesis, and placental development during early pregnancy. In Ayurveda, early fetal demise is described under Garbhapat, attributed to deficient garbhotpadaka bhavas such as inadequate maternal nutrition (ahara rasa).Also uterus is a mamsa dhatu ensures proper tone, thickness, and firmness of the uterine wall, which is essential for receiving and anchoring the fertilized ovum. The inherent mriduta (softness) of healthy mamsa dhatu help uterine tissues to accept the embryo without irritation or rejection, while also protecting it from excessive vata prakopa, a major cause of implantation failure and early pregnancy loss. We report a case of a 20-week missed abortion in a gravida  G5P3L3A1  woman with a significant history of not taking folic acid supplementation, symptoms of anaemia during early pregnancy. Ultrasound revealed a fetus corresponding to 16 weeks with absent cardiac activity, confirming fetal demise. This case highlights the association between folate deficiency and early fetal demise, emphasizing the importance of periconceptional folic acid supplementation for optimal pregnancy outcomes.
In Ayurveda, Rasa dhatu plays a fundamental role in the nourishment and sustenance of pregnancy and its vitiation or depletion is closely related to iron deficiency-associated missed abortion.</jats:p>
